Project `buildsmart-b0b78`. Deploy:
firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes --project buildsmart-b0b78
(firebase.json now points firestore.indexes -> this file).
WHY composite indexes: a query that filters on one field AND orders by
another (or filters on two) needs a composite index — Firestore's automatic
single-field indexes do not cover those. See firestore.rules header 'RULES
ARE NOT FILTERS': a non-manager must SCOPE its listen, and those scoped
queries are exactly the ones indexed here.
Each index below, in order, and its uid-migration state (verified vs repo):
1. orders (contractorUid ASC, ts DESC) — LANDED (uid-A3, commit 24b5bc2).
The contractor scoped listen where('contractorUid'==uid).orderBy('ts'
desc) — newest-first own orders. ACTIVE NOW (contractorUid is written).
2. orders (storeUid ASC, ts DESC) — ACTIVE. storeUid IS written (A4 claim;
orders_firebase toDoc line 86). Serves the store scoped listen's OWN leg
where('storeUid'==uid).orderBy('ts' desc). MUST be storeUid (not storeId)
to match the written field + _ordersScopeFor's store branch — a storeId
index would never serve the storeUid query (failed-precondition).
3. orders (courierUid ASC, ts DESC) — ACTIVE (same as storeUid; toDoc 87).
4. customers (ownerId ASC, used DESC) — FORWARD-READY. ownerId not yet
written; keeps the spend-desc order mgrCustomerList uses for the owner
scoped list once ownerId lands.
5. chatThreads (participantUids ARRAY_CONTAINS, ts DESC) — ACTIVE (A14). The
field is `participantUids` (REAL uids — the auth-truth the rules scope on
and the now-scoped chat listen filters by), NOT `participants` (display
ROLE NAMES). A14 stamps participantUids ⊇ [senderUid] on every touched
thread, so this index serves the uid-scoped listen: where('participantUids',
arrayContains: uid).orderBy('ts' desc) (S4.1). MUST be participantUids (not
participants) to match the written field + the query — a `participants`
index would never serve the participantUids query (failed-precondition).
6. chatMessages (threadId ASC, ts ASC) — ACTIVE NOW. threadId IS written
today; the per-thread stream where('threadId'==id).orderBy('ts') (S4.2)
renders the conversation chronologically (ascending).
7. roleRequests (requestedRole ASC, status ASC) — #6. Serves the approver
list: where('requestedRole'==r).where('status'=='pending') — a contractor
sees worker requests, a store sees courier, a manager sees store+
contractor (an in-list query over the same index). Approve/deny is the
reviewRoleRequest callable; the client sorts the small pending set in-mem.
── Pillar 5 (Scale/Data/Backend · knowledge/studio-plan/05-scale-data-backend.md
§1.5 · Step 52) — 8 NEW composite indexes below (entries 8-15). ALL forward-

8. catalogProducts (tradeId ASC, nameHe ASC) — trade-scoped catalog list, paged:
where('tradeId'==t).orderBy('nameHe').startAfterDocument(cursor).limit(40)
(browse-by-trade; §1.6 cursor pagination — NEVER offset, which bills skipped
docs).
9. catalogProducts (categoryHe ASC, nameHe ASC) — category browse, paged:
where('categoryHe'==c).orderBy('nameHe'). Same cursor pattern as #8.
10. catalogProducts (active ASC, updatedAt DESC) — incremental delta-sync (§7) +
owner 'recently edited': where('active'==true).orderBy('updatedAt' desc).
updatedAt is an ISO-8601 STRING (sorts lexicographically == chrono, like ts).
Step-52 addition-a.
11. catalogProducts (nameTokens ARRAY_CONTAINS, nameHe ASC) — at-scale token
search (§2): where('nameTokens', arrayContains: rarestToken).orderBy('nameHe')
.limit(40), then fuzzySearchProducts re-ranks the small candidate page client-
side. Shape MIRRORS chatThreads #5 (arrayConfig CONTAINS + a trailing order
field) — MUST be nameTokens+nameHe to serve the query, else failed-precondition.
nameTokens are derived server-side from nameHe ONLY (R1-7 — parity with the

12. analyticsEvents (day ASC, name ASC) — owner daily drill-down:
where('day'=='2026-06-23').orderBy('name'). Append-only, owner-read-only
(rules §5); doc-id is auto so writes scatter (no date-partition hotspot).
13. analyticsEvents (uid ASC, at DESC) — per-user support trail:
where('uid'==u).orderBy('at' desc). at is an ISO-8601 STRING.
14. presence (online ASC, lastSeen DESC) — 'who is online now':
where('online'==true).orderBy('lastSeen' desc). Read SERVER-SIDE by the
presenceSummary rollup fn (R1-3 — the owner reads one rolled-up
presenceSummary/current doc, NOT a live listener over every presence doc) and
by the owner's explicit paged drill-down. One self-owned doc/user; TTL sweep
flips stale online->false (§3.4).
15. customers (searchTokens ARRAY_CONTAINS, used DESC) — OPTIONAL customer search
at scale (§1.4): where('searchTokens', arrayContains: tok).orderBy('used'
desc). searchTokens not written yet (forward-ready; same array shape as
studioConfig* need NO composite index — fixed doc-id get/listen only
(studioConfig/published + studioConfig/draft, the ~200B publish pointer; the
tree is a sharded immutable blob read by version, never queried — §1.1, §1.5).
Step-52 addition-b.
NOTE: `ts` is written as an ISO-8601 STRING (orders_firebase toDoc:
createdAt.toIso8601String()); ISO-8601 sorts lexicographically == chrono, so
a string-field DESC/ASC index orders correctly. fieldOverrides is left empty
— every collection keeps its automatic single-field indexes.
